# Stiftung Childaid Network (Childaid Network Foundation)

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-30 · status **complete**

The name 'Child Aid Network Germany' matches Stiftung Childaid Network, a German charitable foundation based in Königstein im Taunus, Germany, founded in 2007 by Dr. Brigitta Cladders and Dr. Martin Kasper. It funds education, child protection, vocational training and health projects for children in South Asia, with its largest and longest-running programme concentrated in Northeast India (mainly Assam, also Manipur, Meghalaya, Nagaland), alongside Nepal, Bangladesh and (small, newer) Myanmar. It is not an Indian Companies Act Section 135 CSR entity — it is a foreign donor foundation that channels German government (BMZ), foundation and private donations to local implementing partners. This is distinct from Kindernothilfe e.V. (KNH), a much larger, separate German child-rights NGO also active in India, whose own website (kindernothilfe.org) could not be read (robots.txt unknown/HELD) — findings below are about Childaid Network only, not Kindernothilfe, and the two should not be merged. Research drew on Childaid Network's 2023 and 2020 annual reports (PDFs) and its Netzkraft partner-network profile. Key findings: total 2023 project spend €3.09 million, of which 66% went to the Northeast India region (vs. 31% Nepal, 3% other) — an explicit percentage, not converted to INR since the source is in EUR and the schema's Money unit only supports inr/lakh/crore. Named India partner NGOs (23, from the 2020 report) include NEAID, The Action Northeast Trust ('the ant'), Bosco Reach Out, Snehalaya, IDeA, Don Bosco University Assam, Pratham/ASER Centre, Quest Alliance, Barefoot College and others — but the 2023 report states some partners have since asked not to be named publicly 'in the context of the developments in India', and that 2023 payments for India projects were blocked by the Indian political/regulatory situation, which is materially relevant to any Indian NGO considering this funder. No open RFP, published grant-size range, or self-service application form was found; partner selection is described as relationship-based (competence, cultural fit, transparency, communication), via existing local partners rather than open calls. No annual report later than the 2023 one (published April 2024) could be located, so no FY2024-25/FY2025-26 figures are available.

Website: https://www.childaid.net

## What it set out to find

- identity: correct legal/registered name, website, entity type, parent (funder)
- identifiers (reg_no, domain, PAN/CIN equivalents)
- csr_year / csr_spend equivalents: latest and prior-year India-directed spend, FY-labelled
- footprint: states/districts where projects actually ran vs stated priority geography
- partners: named Indian implementing NGOs, years, amounts where disclosed
- programs: themes/programmes run
- how to apply: grant size, eligibility, process, open calls, contact point
- documents: annual reports / CSR-equivalent disclosures
- metrics: multi-year income and project-expenditure figures
